findings.title: The 'no client pin / client mismatch' two-wall check is repeated verbatim six times across chatTurn.v23.reads.ts and chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts instead of being hoisted into chatTurn.v23.refusals.ts, the module both files already import shared helpers from
findings.evidence: The identical five-statement shape appears at packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v23.reads.ts:149-162 (runReadPayrollPostingState), :274-287 (runReadPayrollSettlementState), :409-422 (runReadAgreementTerms), and packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:255-268 (runReadRentSettlementCandidates), :466-479 (runConfirmTenancyRentPlan), :644-657 (runConfirmTenancyRentPlanRevision): `if (!ctx.clientId) { return noClientRefusalV23(<reason>, <message>); } if (input.client_id !== ctx.clientId) { return clientMismatchRefusalV23(<reason>, <message>, input.client_id); } const clientId = ctx.clientId;`. Only the two reason tokens and two message strings vary per call site; the control shape, the two refusal constructors invoked and the final rebinding are byte-identical six times. Both files already import `noClientRefusalV23` and `clientMismatchRefusalV23` from chatTurn.v23.refusals.ts, which is the module the tools' own header names as 'the refusal envelope the seven new tools share... a shared helper in either [reads.ts or tenancy.ts] would be a cycle' -- refusals.ts itself has no such cycle risk and is the natural home for the sequencing, not just the two leaf constructors.
findings.why_it_matters: Six independent call sites of the same five-line sequence is the Duplicated Code shape by definition: a future change to the wall's order, its early-return shape, or a new client-scoping rule (e.g. an audit hook, a rate limit) needs six edits instead of one, and the risk is exactly the kind this closure's own docs elsewhere warn about (chatTurn.v23.refusals.ts's header: 'a second copy of an envelope is how two tools in one version come to disagree about what a refusal looks like'). The module already generalises one layer (the two constructors); it stops one layer short of generalising the sequence that calls them.
findings.required_fix: Add one helper to chatTurn.v23.refusals.ts, e.g. `requireClientPin(ctx, inputClientId, noClientReason, noClientMessage, mismatchReason, mismatchMessage): {ok:false,...} | {ok:true, clientId:string}`, and have all six call sites destructure its result instead of repeating the two-branch sequence. Not a same-review blocker -- v23 is a frozen closure and this file is already merged into the diff being reviewed -- but worth taking at the next chatTurn version cut, since every future client-scoped tool in this family will otherwise copy the same six-line block a seventh time.

findings.title: .github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml's new v23 e2e step collapses the file's own one-variable-per-line env convention into a single line with irregular multi-space gaps, unlike every neighbouring block in the same file including the v22 block immediately above it
findings.evidence: action.yml:443-457 (the v22 block, kept unchanged): `PGPORT=$PGC_PORT \` / `PGDATABASE=clara_wave_b_ci \` / `RELAY_TEST_MODE=1 \` / `WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="..." \` / `  node "..." tests/chat-turn-v22-e2e.mjs`, one assignment per line with a backslash continuation. The new v23 line directly below it (action.yml:457, per `git diff ffb629d73...HEAD -- .github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml`) instead reads as one physical line: `PGPORT=$PGC_PORT         PGDATABASE=clara_wave_b_ci         RELAY_TEST_MODE=1         WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://postgres@localhost:$PGC_PORT/clara_wave_b_ci"           node "..." tests/chat-turn-v23-e2e.mjs`, with runs of 8-11 literal spaces where the sibling block has newlines-plus-backslash.
findings.why_it_matters: Bash still parses the collapsed line correctly (whitespace-separated env assignments before a command are equivalent whichever way the line wraps), and the driver behind it (world-gate.mjs on tests/chat-turn-v23-e2e.mjs) is exercised and passes, so this is cosmetic only -- not a functional defect and not something CI would catch. It is a real, visible deviation from the file's own established convention in the very same file for the very same list of four variables, most likely an artifact of how the multi-line block was pasted, and it is the kind of hunk a future diff of this file will misread as a meaningful change.
findings.required_fix: Reformat the new step's env assignment to the file's own one-per-line backslash-continuation style, matching the v22 block immediately above it. Purely cosmetic; safe to fold into any future touch of this file rather than a same-review blocker.

summary: #1144's diff is unusually disciplined against this repo's own frozen-workflow law: zero edits to any deploy-locked v22/v6 source file, the registry's five-edit-per-class shape followed exactly, check-frozen-workflows/--compare-base/parts-parity/worker-paths and CI=true lint all re-run clean and matching the report's own claims, and the one genuinely load-bearing new predicate (loadFaProposalInputsStepV7's six-condition completeness check) independently verified byte-for-byte against the live database function it claims as its source of truth. TDD vertical-slice discipline holds at commit granularity across all 9 commits, including a real red-then-green cycle in the e2e-walk commit that found and fixed an actual defect (a lost detail.reason on a door-sent CLR11). The two findings filed are both judgement-call smells, not standards violations: a six-times-repeated client-pin/mismatch check that the closure's own refusals module could absorb (STD-1, minor), and a cosmetic single-line collapse of the file's own established multi-line env-var convention in one CI YAML hunk (STD-2, note). Neither blocks acceptance.
